conclusions: The Info-capable automation API produced a complete lossless HMD-stereo sequence without Developer Mode or Debug logging.
The five-frame combined-stereo average had descriptive raw sRGB channel means [26.2482, 22.8153, 22.3762].
Its mean-image absolute difference from the all-on reference was 1.8606 8-bit code values, above the 0.3874-0.4930 within-condition mean absolute deviation observed in this campaign.
Disabling Volumetric Shadows makes deep timber, the walkway, and foreground stone darker and harder-edged, while the distant cliff-haze region becomes markedly darker and clearer in this capture.

The observed surface change is consistent with the implementation's broad reach: its filtered directional variance-shadow map is consumed by ordinary Lighting as well as volumetric, particle, effect, and water paths. The toggle is not only a fog-quality switch.
The picture set is suitable for human/LLM review and for designing more deterministic shader-isolation scenes.
notes: One preparatory stereo pair warmed the capture path.
Image statistics used five combined-stereo frames per candidate, downsampled to 756x420 without linear-light conversion; they are descriptive rather than perceptual or attribution metrics.
IBL EnableIBL and Volumetric Shadows Enabled are audited as live renderer controls, but this campaign restarted because typed API mutation and effective-state readback are not implemented yet.
